The main takeaway from our work is that

the beta2 microglobin mutant is able to crystallize in a tetragonal form, which has been previously observed in the wild type only in the presence of copper ions, and in a different crystal environment.

the tetrameric form is stabilized by intermolecular hydrogen bonding between the C-terminal residues of the protein molecules, which are involved in the copper-binding site of the wild-type beta2 microglobulins.
